ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, if $A$ represents the area of the square, what is the value of $A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the side length of the square represented by A be $x$,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem we have $x^{2}+3^{2}=5^{2}$,\\
$\therefore x^{2}=16,$ which means the area of the square represented by A is $\boxed{16}$.

The triangle has another leg labeled 3, a hypotenuse labeled 5, and the right-angle mark shows the square side and the 3-side are perpendicular.
